text.p: Hungarian mineral water bottler and distributor Kekkuti Asvanyviz Rt's shareholders on Thursday decided not to pay dividend on 1996 earnings but from 1997 the company intends to do so, a company official said.

"Bourse listing of our shares began last December and our shareholders decided not to pay dividend this (1996) year," company finance director Karoly Telegdi told Reuters after Kekkuti's annual general meeting.
"From 1997 on, however, one can expect that about 10 percent of the after-tax profit will be spent on dividends and on the buy-back of own shares."
Kekkuti announced in a statement this morning it had decided to buy own shares up to a nominal 11.9 million forints which is equal to five percent of its issued share capital.

When asked about the 1997 plans Telegdi said only that the company plans to boost its sales and profits by at least 30 percent this year and plans to increase its domestic market share of around 22 to 25 percent.
"We would like at least to maintain this position, but possibly to raise it," he said.
"If the summer weather will be at least average unlikely last year when it was unfavourable we would like to reach an increase of at least 30 percent in both sales and profits."
In 1996 Kekkuti had HAS sales revenues of 1.165 billion forints.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Kekkuti shares traded at 1,200 forints, up 50, at 1031 GMT.
